facts: This is an application for leave to appeal u/art. 136 of the constitution from the decision and judgment of the High court of Orissa, dated April 8, 1967.
In or about 1975-76 the respondent was entrusted with the work of 'construction of balance work of earth dam of Koska Minor Irrigation Project'
Final bill was prepared on February 12, 1980 and it was unconditionally accepted by the respondent-contractor.
On or about April 16, 1980, the respondent-contractor raised certain claims and gave notice for appointment of an arbitrator according to the contract.
Before the arbitrator the respondent filed its claim along with some documents and the petitioner filed his counter-statement.
issues: Whether there is an error of law apparent on the face of the award
Whether the arbitrator has misconducted himself by giving a lump sum award without examining each item of the claims

Whether the claimant having accepted the final bill unconditionally deposit, the contract between the parties stood closed and, therefore, the arbitration clause was not operative and the arbitrator appointed had no jurisdiction to adjudicate upon the disputes
Whether the award of interest is without jurisdiction
petitioner_arguments: The fact that there is an unreasoned award, is no ground to set aside an award.
Lump sum award is not bad per se, as such.

An award may be set aside by the court on the ground of error on the face of the award, but an award is not invalid merely because by a process of inference and argument it may be demonstrated that the arbitrator has committed some mistake in arriving at his conclusion.
court_reasoning: The High Court was right in refusing to accept the challenge to the award.

An award is conclusive as a judgment between the parties and the court is entitled to set aside an award only if the arbitrator has misconducted himself in the proceedings or when the award has been made after the issue of an order by the court superseding the arbitration or after arbitration proceedings have become invalid u/s. 35 of the Arbitration Act or where an award has been improperly procured or is otherwise invalid u/s. 30 of the Act.

An award may be set aside by the court on the ground of error on the face of the award, but an award is not invalid merely because by a process of inference and argument it may be demonstrated that the arbitrator has committed some mistake in arriving at his conclusion.
holding: The application fails and is accordingly dismissed.
